facts.name: Zigzag Goldenrod
facts.light: Part shade to shade; average soil
facts.notes: A goldenrod that is happy in shade, named for its zigzag stems. Its pollen is carried mostly by insects rather than wind. Spreads slowly.

companions.why: New Moon Nurseries: at a woods edge, try pairing zigzag goldenrod with heart-leaved aster (Aster cordifolius).
Minnesota Board of Water and Soil Resources: good companion plants include early meadow rue, wild columbine and zigzag goldenrod.
